name: Dark circles method

lead: The dark circles method is a forum-popularised way of approaching under-eye darkness by first working out what is causing it. Under-eye darkness can come from visible blood vessels through thin skin, from extra pigment, from allergies or poor sleep, or from shadows cast by the underlying bone structure, and each cause has a different fix.

The appearance payoff is a brighter, more rested-looking eye area. Dermatology overviews list topical caffeine, vitamin C, fillers, lasers and concealer among the options; the forum version of the method packages these into a decision tree.

paras: People first sort their dark circles into vascular, pigment, allergy-related or structural types. Forum advice suggests topical caffeine for circulation-related circles, treating allergies where relevant, retinol or tyrosinase inhibitors such as vitamin C or alpha arbutin for pigment, and concealer or filler where bone shadowing is the cause. Eye-area products are preferred to limit irritation.

Retinol and acids can irritate the thin skin around the eyes. Filler near the lower lid carries the risks of any injectable, including swelling, lumps and rare vascular complications, and should be done by a qualified clinician. Hydroquinone, once used for pigment, was withdrawn from over-the-counter use in the US in 2006 and is restricted in Europe.

chain: Identify the type of dark circle
Apply the matching topical, makeup or filler approach
angle.text: The method aims to lighten or camouflage the area beneath the eyes so the face looks rested. Cause matters because pigment, vessels and bone shadows respond to different products.

lead: The dark circles method is a framework discussed on looksmax.org for reducing periorbital darkness by diagnosing its cause before choosing a treatment [1].

One widely quoted forum answer divides dark circles into groups. When they stem from poor circulation or bad sleep, a vasoconstrictor such as topical caffeine is suggested; when allergies are responsible, treating the allergy is suggested; for excess pigment, retinol and tyrosinase inhibitors such as vitamin C or alpha arbutin are suggested; and when bone structure creates shadowing, concealer makeup or filler are the options mentioned [1]. Another contributor adds that puffy eyebags differ from dark circles and that salt before bed is reported to increase puffiness [1].
Medical references describe a similar spread of causes, including thin lower-eyelid skin, heredity, allergies and eye rubbing, sun exposure, ageing and nutritional factors [2].
infobox: Caffeine, vitamin C, retinol, alpha arbutin
Concealer, filler, laser, fat transfer, implants

paras: The method is less a product than a decision tree. A forum thread titled around the method lists causes and a matching approach for each, and a thread participant asks whether infraorbital rim implants belong on the list while another replies that the thread concerns softer options [1]. One user in the thread mentions having deliberated for six years between an implant and fat graft [1].

Reference sources list anatomy (bone structure and the thin skin of the lower eyelid), allergies and eczema, medications that dilate vessels, fatigue, ageing and sun-driven pigment as contributors [2].

Topical caffeine is described as a vasoconstrictor reported to improve appearance, and vitamin C is described as brightening pigment, with a 2009 study cited for the latter [2]. Laser or intense pulsed light, low-level laser therapy, fat transfer and hyaluronic acid filler are listed as procedural options [2].

Hydroquinone, once common in lightening creams, had its US over-the-counter approval revoked in 2006 and is banned in European countries [2]. Forum users recommend eye-specific products to avoid irritation [1].
No studies found on the method as a whole. Individual ingredients and procedures such as vitamin C, caffeine, lasers and fillers have been studied for periorbital hyperpigmentation [2].

lore.intro: Dark circles are a recurring topic on looksmax.org, where users share product names and sort causes into vascular, pigment and structural groups [1].

claims.claim: The right fix depends on the cause of the circles.
Caffeine creams constrict vessels and reduce vascular dark circles.
Structural dark circles from bone shadowing can only be hidden or filled.
